subject: Renewal: propose stepped commit + temporary price-hold for surge
messages:
From: Evan Morales <evan@atlasretail.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal discussion — usage spike and options

Hi Marcus,

Quick heads up: our renewal is up at the end of September and consumption has grown ~2.8x since we signed. We love Redwood's latency and tooling, but this surge has blown past our expected commit. Procurement asked whether you can hold current pricing for a short period while we lock in a new commit — ideally a 6 month price-hold for any overage beyond the new commit so we can plan capacity.

Also asking for a modest onboarding/feature credit to cover integration work for a new storefront rollout. Can you share what levers you have (short-term price-hold, credits, phased commit levels, or term adjustments) so we can present options to our CFO?

Thanks — Evan
Evan Morales
Head of Platform, Atlas Retail
E: evan@atlasretail.com
A: procurement@atlasretail.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Morales <evan@atlasretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — usage spike and options

Evan — thanks for the context and congrats on the product launch traction. High level options we can move quickly on: 

- Option A (Conservative): 12-month renewal with a stepped commit. 10% discounted rate on committed token consumption; overages billed at current list but we offer a 3-month temporary price-hold for surge overages (applies only to spike months and capped at 50% of overage).
- Option B (Growth): 18-month renewal; higher commit two-step (year 1 = 1.25x current run-rate, year 2 = 1.8x) with a 6-month price-hold on overages and a one-time $25,000 onboarding credit to offset integration.
- Option C (Short-term bridge): 6 month bridge extension at current pricing + $15k credit, followed by a reprice based on observed trailing 3-month consumption.

Attached: Atlas_Renewal_Proposal_v1.pdf with line-items and unit economics. If you prefer, I can propose a hybrid (9-month price-hold + smaller upfront credit) tied to a short commitment uplift.

Next steps: Evan, tell me which option you want us to firm up and I will loop Legal/Finance for a redline. Ben/Naomi — can you surface any margin constraints if we offer a 6-month hold + $25k credit?

Best,
Marcus Lin
Enterprise Account Lead — Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — margin check and SLA ask

Marcus — looping Finance. Naomi: can we entertain Option B (18 mo with stepped uplift + $25k credit and 6-month price hold) from a margin perspective? Primary asks from Sales: 6-month overage price-hold and $25k one-time credit. Also recommend we include an SLA credit schedule (latency > SLA thresholds) to sweeten the extension but protect us operationally.

I attached a quick margin model (renewal-margin-calc.xlsx) with back-of-envelope impact at several uplift scenarios. If we need to limit the price-hold, suggest capping at 3 months or limiting to X% of monthly overage.

If Finance signs off, I can draft the redline to legal and send a tracked PDF to Evan's procurement team.

Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager — Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Evan Morales <evan@atlasretail.com>, procurement@atlasretail.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — proposal & next steps

Evan — appreciate the quick cadence. Update after internal review: Finance is okay to move on a middle-ground that balances your operational runway and our unit economics. 

Proposed counter (summary):
- 15-month term (to align with your fiscal cadence)
- Stepped commit: months 1-6 = 1.25x current run-rate, months 7-15 = 1.8x current run-rate
- One-time onboarding credit: $20,000 (applied to first invoice)
- Temporary price-hold: 9 months of protection on overage pricing (applies to contiguous spike months; cap = 40% of monthly overage)
- SLA credit: included for latency/availability breaches as a commercial remedy (language to be added by Legal)

Attachments: Atlas_Renewal_Counter_v2.pdf (tracked redline). DocuSign link to follow once procurement confirms intent: https://app.docusign.com/prepare/ABC12345

If this package looks reasonable, can you confirm by EOD Monday so we can get Legal to issue a redline and procurement to route the PO? If you need a stronger short-term hold (e.g., full 6 month at 0% overage), we could consider that as a conditional concession in exchange for an additional firmed commit or a prepay.

Thanks — happy to hop on a 20 minute call to walk through the numbers.

Marcus Lin
Enterprise Account Lead — Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192
